content:
Apple has officially launched a new product rental program called "Apple Upgrade," which is now available in the United States starting today.

Apple Upgrade is powered by Klarna, allowing users to rent-to-own iPhones, Apple Watches, Macs, and iPads, with the option to easily upgrade at the end of the lease term. Here's how it works.

Apple Upgrade Rental Program: How It Works

Apple Upgrade covers Apple's entire product lineup, including the latest iPhone 17 series, MacBook Air, Apple Watch Series 11, and more.

iPhone and Apple Watch leases are available in 12-month and 24-month terms; Mac and iPad leases are available in 24-month and 36-month terms.

  • iPhone leases start at US$17.99 per month, based on the iPhone 17e.
  • Apple Watch leases start at US$11.99 per month, based on the Apple Watch Series 11.
  • Mac leases start at US$24.99 per month, based on the MacBook Air.
  • iPad leases start at US$15.99 per month, based on the iPad mini.

Apple Upgrade has been integrated into the checkout process on Apple's website, appearing alongside other purchasing options. During the process, users can also trade in their old devices to lower the monthly fee during the initial lease term, including Apple devices and Android phones.

After configuring the device and selecting Apple Upgrade, the system will conduct a soft credit check to assess eligibility, which will not affect your credit score.

The program is powered by Klarna, which will handle payments and credit approval on Apple's behalf. Once enrolled in Apple Upgrade, users can manage all payment information, due dates, and other details through the Klarna app.

Apple Upgrade does not include AppleCare by default, but users can add it for an additional monthly fee, or add the device to an existing AppleCare One bundle.

You can visit Apple's website for all pricing information. Below are highlights of monthly fees for selected Apple devices through the Apple Upgrade program:

  • iPhone 17 Pro 256GB (US$1,099): US$31.99 per month for 24 months, or US$45.99 per month for 12 months
  • Apple Watch Series 11 GPS, 42mm (US$399): US$11.99 per month for 24 months, or US$21.99 per month for 12 months
  • iPad Pro 256GB (US$1,199): US$24.99 per month for 36 months, or US$31.99 per month for 24 months
  • MacBook Pro 16GB RAM / 1TB storage (US$1,999): US$38.99 per month for 36 months, or US$53.99 per month for 24 months

At the end of the lease term, you can choose to upgrade to a new device, purchase your current device outright, or return the device and exit the program entirely. If you choose to buy out the device, you must pay the difference between the amount already paid and the product's retail price.

All three options are available from day one. For example, you can upgrade early or exit the program early by paying off the remaining balance. The program does not charge any other fees or interest.

The following devices are not eligible for the Apple Upgrade program:

  • iPhone 16
  • iPhone 16 Plus
  • Apple Watch SE
  • MacBook Neo
  • Mac mini
  • iPad (A16)
  • Studio Display

Below are additional things to know about Apple Upgrade:

  • iPhone leases require service from AT&T, T-Mobile, or Verizon; prepaid plans are not accepted. The iPhone is unlocked, and users can switch carriers at any time.
  • The first payment is due approximately 30 days after the device ships or becomes available for pickup.
  • Paying lease fees with an Apple Card earns 3% Daily Cash.
  • Apple Upgrade is not eligible for education pricing.
  • If no action is taken at the end of the lease term, the lease will convert to a month-to-month renewal for up to six months, with the monthly fee potentially increasing. After this period, the device buyout price will be charged. You will not own the device unless this amount is paid.
  • If a payment is missed, the amount will roll over to the next billing cycle with no late fees. If three consecutive payments are missed, the lease agreement will be terminated, and you must pay the entire outstanding balance.

Finally, with the launch of Apple Upgrade, Apple will discontinue the iPhone Upgrade Program and iPhone Payments installment plan. Existing iPhone Upgrade Program customers can continue using their current plan until they're ready to upgrade, then switch to the new program's options.

Apple Upgrade is available for applications starting today on Apple's website, the Apple Store app, and Apple Store retail locations.
